decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “Saving… bookmarks.” Round 1 client (entry 2) describes pasting a web address as the intended save flow.
decisions.note: The baseline includes URL-based bookmark saving; specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “deleting bookmarks.” No contrary behavior is presented.
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion conforms at the baseline specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “tagging… bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Assigning tags is recorded as supported; specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “Duplicate-link prevention.” Round 5 client (entry 10): duplicate saves “stop me and point me at the one I've got,” including capitalization and trailing-slash variants.
decisions.note: The presented duplicate-prevention behavior converges on the existing bookmark; confirmed at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) only says “viewing” bookmarks; no presentation or response establishes the displayed fields or whether selecting an item opens the original URL.
decisions.note: The recorded viewing decision is too underspecified to establish conformity or divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) says “editing” bookmarks, and round 4 maker (entry 7) lists “Editing,” but the transcript never establishes editing all required URL/title/description/tags/note fields.
decisions.note: Generic editing is presented, but its complete field scope cannot be judged.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1): “Search and filtering.” Round 3 maker (entry 5): “SQLite with full-text search.” Neither presentation nor client response identifies all indexed fields or case-insensitive behavior.
decisions.note: The full-text search field coverage and case rule remain unverifiable across specification and planning.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) presents the baseline; round 1 client (entry 2) says it requires typing the title and excludes automatic retrieval, calls that “a miss,” and asks the app to grab the page name, description, and icon.
decisions.note: The client replaces a manual/omitted metadata workflow with automatic collection; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) omits read-later behavior. Round 1 client (entry 2) requests a flag, a list showing only those items, and the ability to check them off after reading.
decisions.note: The client adds the missing unread flag, unread-only view, and mark-read behavior; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) offers deletion but no archive. Round 1 client (entry 2) asks to “tuck a bookmark away without deleting it” so it leaves the normal list but can be recovered.
decisions.note: The client adds reversible archiving and explicitly distinguishes it from permanent deletion; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client (entry 2) identifies the maker's decision directly: “You've listed sorting as out of scope,” then requests ordering by name or date.
decisions.note: The client rejects the sorting exclusion and supplies conforming sort keys; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client (entry 2) contrasts the presented “plain word matching” with the expected ability to search an exact phrase.
decisions.note: The client corrects the limited search behavior by specifying exact-phrase matching; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) explicitly excludes “imports/exports.” Round 1 client (entry 2) asks to bring in existing bookmarks rather than rule importing out.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing import capability; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker (entry 1) explicitly excludes “imports/exports.” Round 1 client (entry 2) says they want to bring bookmarks in “and get them back out.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing export capability; initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) defers page snapshots as a follow-up. Round 2 client (entry 4) identifies the expected “saved copies of pages” and says “I'm fine with your plan… handling it properly on its own later.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly recognizes and accepts deferral of local page snapshots; specification gate. The earlier request to discuss it is linked here and not counted separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) narrows automatic retrieval to “title, description, and site-icon,” omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client (entry 4) repeats only title, description, and icon and approves it as “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised metadata decision remains divergent because preview-image collection is absent; the response never identifies that difference. Revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) presents automatic metadata with “editable previews,” while the retained baseline includes editing. Round 2 client (entry 4) confirms the returned fields can be tweaked.
decisions.note: Editable metadata before saving, together with ordinary editing afterward, conforms at the revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “A read-later queue with read/unread status.” Round 2 client (entry 4) confirms “the read-later list with marking things read.”
decisions.note: The revised read-later behavior conforms; revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Reversible archive and restore.” Round 2 client (entry 4) confirms “set-aside-and-restore for archiving.”
decisions.note: Reversible archive, distinct from deletion, conforms at the revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 2 and 5 maker (entries 3 and 9) present “archive and restore.” The clients say archived items leave the normal view and can be restored, but neither side establishes an archived-only list.
decisions.note: The archive-only perspective cannot be confirmed or disproved from the recorded presentations and responses.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Sorting by title or date in either direction.” Round 2 client (entry 4) explicitly confirms sorting by name or date.
decisions.note: The revised sorting decision conforms; revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3): “Exact-phrase search.” Round 2 client (entry 4) confirms it matches the intended behavior.
decisions.note: Exact-phrase search conforms at the revised specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) presents “combined tag/state filters”; round 2 client (entry 4) confirms narrowing by more than one tag.
decisions.note: Filtering by selected tags includes the required single-tag filtering behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) defines smarter search as exact phrases plus combined tag/state filters; round 5 maker (entry 9) again lists only “phrase and multi-tag search.” Clients in entries 4, 6, 8, and 10 approve those modes without mentioning `#tag` syntax, Boolean operators, parentheses, or literal-operator quoting.
decisions.note: The presented search scope omits the reference's tag-search syntax and Boolean/grouping grammar; repeated approvals do not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) promises imports from major-browser bookmark exports; round 5 client (entry 10) only confirms “the import is there.” The transcript does not establish preservation of title, tags, and date-added.
decisions.note: The import format is plausibly browser-compatible, but required field preservation cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker (entry 3) presents “Complete export and restoration of app-specific data,” rather than a browser/Netscape HTML export. Round 2 client (entry 4) approves being able to get the collection back out without identifying the format difference.
decisions.note: The round-2 export decision is app-specific and therefore diverges from the required interchange format; the client does not surface that mismatch.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client (entry 4) asks whether typing a tag suggests existing tags. Round 3 maker (entry 5) says this is “explicitly included,” and round 3 client (entry 6) says the loose end “is handled.”
decisions.note: Linked clarification establishes that autocomplete already conformed; it is not an unresolved or corrective divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker (entry 5) presents “Browser-compatible HTML export plus lossless JSON backups.” Round 3 client (entry 6) explicitly approves the browser-friendly bookmark file.
decisions.note: The later browser-compatible HTML export is functionally equivalent to Netscape bookmark HTML; planning gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) reports read later implemented. Round 5 client (entry 10) verifies that the list shows only unread items and marking one read removes it.
decisions.note: Implementation-review evidence confirms the complete read-later behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) reports archive/restore implemented. Round 5 client (entry 10) verifies archiving removes items from the normal view without deleting them and restoration works.
decisions.note: Implementation-review evidence confirms reversible archiving distinct from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) reports phrase and multi-tag search plus sorting. Round 5 client (entry 10) verifies multi-tag filtering, quoted exact phrases, and sorting by name or date in both directions.
decisions.note: These implemented filter, phrase-search, and sorting decisions conform at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) reports tag suggestions implemented; round 5 client (entry 10) confirms “the tag suggestions I asked about are there.”
decisions.note: Autocomplete is confirmed at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9) reports browser exports; round 5 client (entry 10) verifies a “browser-friendly file” export alongside the separate full backup.
decisions.note: The implemented browser-bookmark export conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker (entry 9): “Saved page copies remain documented as the next separately specified feature.” Round 5 client (entry 10): “Saved copies of pages we already agreed to hold for a later round, so I'm not counting that against this.”
decisions.note: At implementation review, the client again explicitly recognizes and accepts the still-deferred snapshot requirement.
